govdocs-archive_org-jors195320fppng_v03_: Vannevar Bush’s Research and the War Effort — from a 1953 filmstrip — tells how Yankee science served World War II. The OSRD chief’s tale covers radar, the bomb, and penicillin. His vision shaped postwar science. The book is a landmark of science-policy history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HochPaulHSCANot: Paul L. Hoch’s Comments on the House Assassinations Committee Hearings is a researcher’s take. Hoch was a meticulous researcher. His notes are sharp. The hearings aired the evidence. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
the-arctic-prairies-a-canoe-journey-of-2: Naturalist Ernest Thompson Seton — founder of the Woodcraft movement — canoed 2,000 miles through Canada's barren lands searching for the caribou herds. His account of wildlife, Indigenous guides, and vast northern spaces is a classic of wilderness writing. Adventure and natural history in one magnificent journey.
indian-games-an-historical-research: Andrew McFarland Davis investigates the games of Native American peoples — their ball games, dice, and contests of skill — as serious historical evidence of culture. His pioneering research shows play as a window into how societies live and think. A foundational study in the anthropology of sport.
the-true-story-of-my-life-a-sketch: Hans Christian Andersen tells his own fairy tale — the poor cobbler's son who became Denmark's beloved storyteller. His autobiographical sketch is as charming as his stories, full of struggle, luck, and gratitude. The man behind the Little Mermaid and the Ugly Duckling, in his own modest words.
indian-frontier-policy-an-historical-ske: Sir John Adye, soldier and ruler in India, sketches Britain's policy on the wild Northwest Frontier — the hard choices of guarding an empire's edge against Russia. His inside view throws light on how imperial plans were made, and what they cost. Short, clear, and most revealing.
catherine-booth-a-sketch: Mildred Duff sketches the life of Catherine Booth — the Mother of the Salvation Army, preacher and reformer. Her courage beside her husband William changed countless lives. A brief, inspiring tribute to a great woman. Wife, mother, and preacher, she carried the Army's flag into the darkest streets.
jack-ranger-s-western-trip-or-from-board: Clarence Young's Jack Ranger takes a western trip — from boarding school to ranch and range — in this lively series tale. Cowboys, cattle, and boyish fun fill the pages. A rattling good Western for boys who love the open range. Bronco busting and cattle drives test the schoolboys' grit.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-echt: This 1913 Catholic reference piece on Echternach — St. Willibrord's house, home of the hopping saints' day march — tells its bright story. George Cyprian Alston covers its fame. Pilgrims still dance to the saint's tomb at Whitsun. Willibrord, the English saint, rests in its crypt.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-achimelech: This 1913 reference piece on Achimelech — the priest of Nob, slain for aiding David. Wendell Reilly recounts the massacre. Eighty-five priests fell by Saul's order. Hospitality punished with death. The shewbread he gave David became Gospel proof. Doeg's sword did Saul's cruel work.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adrian-and-pe: A 1913 entry on Adrian and Peter von Walenburch — the Dutch brothers who debated Protestants. Friedrich Lauchert honors their controversial skill. Cologne's press spread their arguments. Two pens for the old faith. The Reformation's Catholic answer. Their tracts filled the controversial libraries.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aldersbach: This 1913 reference piece on Aldersbach — the Bavarian Cistercian abbey. Henry Brock tells its long story. Its church glows with Baroque art. Monks prayed here for seven centuries. A jewel of the Bavarian plain. Its brewery is famed as its church.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ambo-in-the-r: This 1913 reference article on the ambo in the Russian and Greek church — the raised reading place. Andrew Shipman describes its solemn use. The deacon sings the Gospel from its height. The people hear the word uplifted. The East's pulpit of stone.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amorbach: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Amorbach — the Bavarian Benedictine abbey. Henry Brock tells its long story. Its church glows with Baroque splendor. Monks prayed here for a thousand years. A jewel of the Odenwald. Its organ is famed through Franconia.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-dioce: This 1913 reference article on the ancient diocese of Norwich — the see of East Anglia. Edwin Burton traces its bishops. Thetford and Elmham came before it. Its cathedral spire crowns the city. A great medieval diocese. Its close keeps the medieval houses.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antioch: A 1913 entry on Antioch — the great patriarchate of the East. Edward Arbez tells its apostolic glory. There the disciples were first called Christians. Its school shaped the ancient theology. The queen of the Eastern sees. Its patriarchs ruled the Christian East.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antiphon-in-t: This 1913 reference article on the antiphon in the Greek Church — its festal use. Andrew Shipman notes its solemn place. The great feasts multiply their number. The chant crowns the celebration. The Church's sung ornament. Their number grows on the great feasts.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anton-ulrich: This 1913 reference article on Anton Ulrich — the Duke of Brunswick who turned Catholic. Thomas Shahan tells his conversion's tale. His court at Wolfenbüttel shone with art. The convert prince edified the Empire. A duke who chose Rome. His library was Europe's wonder.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arch: A 1913 entry on the arch in architecture — the curve that carries the weight. Thomas Poole explains its structural art. Rome perfected the semicircular span. The Gothic pointed it to heaven. The backbone of the builders' craft. Its keystone locks the curving stones.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-auch: A 1913 entry on Auch — the Gascon archdiocese. Georges Goyau gives its story. Its cathedral crowns the Gers. The Armagnac counts ruled its lands. A see of the southwest. Its choir stalls are a Gothic wonder. Its archbishops crowned the Gascon church.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-auzias-march: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Ausiàs March — the great Catalan poet. Jeremiah Ford honors his brooding verse. His cantos sang of love and death. Valencia's court heard his lyre. The Petrarch of the Catalan tongue. His manuscripts rest in Valencia's library.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-baruch: A 1913 entry on Baruch — Jeremiah's scribe and the book that bears his name. Francis Gigot weighs its sacred text. His pen saved the prophet's words. The exiles read his consolations. The scribe of the weeping prophet. His letter consoles the exiled Jews.
